Welcome to Avishayes Primary School
The choice of school for your child is a very important one. We hope that you will find the information in this website helpful. We are very proud of our Curriculum, Teaching and Learning. If you would like the opportunity to look around the school, please call to arrange a visit between 3:30pm and 4:30pm to have a tour of the site with a member of the senior leadership team.
All the staff at Avishayes bring great commitment and professionalism to their jobs of teaching and caring for children. If you decide to choose our school for your child, we look forward to working with you and hope that you and your child will be very happy.
Learning at Avishayes
Curriculum
Our broad, balanced and inspiring curriculum helps every child develop curiosity, confidence and a love of learning across all subjects.
Author
From phonics to storytelling, we build strong communication skills, a love of reading, and confidence in speaking and writing.
Mathematician
We nurture mathematical thinkers who can reason, problem-solve and see the patterns that shape the world around them.
Scientist
Hands-on experiments spark curiosity and discovery, helping children explore how and why things work in the world around them.
Historian and Geographer
We inspire curiosity about people, places and the past – helping children understand their world and their place within it.
Musician
Each year-group has at least one half-term to explore their creativity through art, dance, music or drama.
Athlete
Through sport and active play, children build teamwork, fitness and confidence - developing healthy habits for life.
Philosopher
Our PSHE curriculum promotes kindness, resilience and respect – supporting every child’s wellbeing and personal growth.
Engineer and ICT
Children become confident digital learners – using technology safely, creatively and responsibly to enhance learning.
Avishayes Primary School and Early Years Centre has strengths in Early Years, Behaviours and Attitudes and Personal Development.
(Ofsted October 2024)
The school strongly promotes the pupils’ spiritual, moral, social and cultural development through a wide range of stimulating activities. This underpins the very supportive relationships between adults and pupils and between pupils that enrich their enjoyment and increased efforts in learning.
All groups of pupils, including disabled pupils, those with special educational needs and the most able, relish their learning. This is because teachers and teaching assistants set work and question them effectively to extend their thinking and skills.

Aims & Values
At Avishayes we are determined to create an inclusive culture of learning where all children will aim high and be challenged to achieve to the best of their abilities. We aim to nurture a life-long love of learning by developing independent learners; to develop children’s emotional health and empower our children to become respected citizens enabling them to make valuable contributions locally, nationally and globally.
It is our intention that children develop knowledge and skills in these areas:
At Avishayes, we believe every child should feel they belong, be valued for who they are and be inspired to achieve beyond what they thought possible.
Our inclusive community celebrates diversity, removes barriers to learning and ensures every child is supported, challenged and empowered to flourish. We recognise that every learner has unique strengths, talents and aspirations, and we are committed to helping each child discover and develop them.
As we look to the future, we will place oracy and mathematics at the heart of our curriculum. We believe that the ability to communicate with confidence, think critically, reason logically and solve problems creatively will be the defining skills of tomorrow's world. In an age of rapid technological change and artificial intelligence, children will need to articulate their ideas, collaborate effectively, analyse information and make informed decisions with confidence.
Through high-quality teaching and rich learning experiences, we will develop articulate communicators, resilient problem-solvers and curious learners who are equipped to thrive in education, employment and life. By combining strong relationships, ambitious expectations and an inclusive culture, we will ensure every child leaves Avishayes with the knowledge, confidence and character to make a positive contribution to their community and beyond.

About Avishayes
Welcome to Avishayes
Avishayes Primary School & Early Years Centre
At Avishayes Primary School & Early Years Centre, we proudly live by our motto: “Aim High – Achieve Together.” Nestled in Chard, Somerset, we are welcoming and inclusive learning community serving children ages 3 to 11.
Our Vision & Values
We believe every child has the potential to flourish academically, socially and personally. Through our broad and engaging curriculum, including Early Years, primary years and the nurturing wrap-around of our Early Years Centre, we support children to become confident, curious, kind and resilient learners.
High expectations for effort and achievement
Strong relationships and mutual respect
Learning together in a safe, supportive environment
What We Offer
Early Years Centre
A welcoming start where children aged 3–5 explore, play and learn with confidence and curiosity in a stimulating environment.
Primary School
A one-form entry school where each child is known, valued and supported to grow academically and personally.
Inclusive Support
We are fully inclusive, offering tailored support for children with special educational needs and/or disabilities – working closely with families and external services.
Our Community
At Avishayes, school is not just about what happens in the classroom – it is about the whole community working together. We value strong partnerships with parents, carers and local organisations. We believe that when school and home work hand in hand, children thrive.
Our school culture fosters kindness, respect and a sense of belonging – where every child can feel safe to ask questions, make mistakes and aim high.
Leadership & Staff
Our dedicated staff bring professionalism, commitment and heart to their roles. From Early Years through to Year 6, our teams work collaboratively to ensure learning is tailored, meaningful and joyful.
As Headteacher Mrs Clare Rinaldi notes, "We look forward to working with you and hope that you and your child will be very happy here."
Let’s Learn Together
Choosing the right school is a big decision. We warmly invite you to visit Avishayes to feel the energy, meet the staff, and see first-hand how we foster a love of learning. Tours can be arranged between 3:30 pm and 4:30 pm. Contact us to schedule your visit.
We are proud of our achievements, but even more excited about what lies ahead for our children. At Avishayes, we aim high and together we achieve.

Humanities Development
Humanities Development
We want our children to be curious about people, places and times past and present. We use our local community to find out more. Through their enquiry 'How do we find out about people from the past?' Year 3 visit the Chard Museum every week for 5 weeks. Each week they look at a different aspect of historical sources. In July 2023 Year 3 children were interviewed and described their 'Museum in a Box' for the Chard Cast Podcasts. 'My Home is My Museum' was a collaborative project with Chard Museum funded through Culturally Chard.
In Year 6 the children learn all about Ancient Greece with Konflux Theatre's Play in a day. Children gain knowledge through real experiences built up over time.

Forest School
Forest School & Activities
Forest School is a unique way of building independence and self-esteem. It originated in Sweden as a way of teaching children about the natural world. The Forest School ethos focuses on developing emotional and social benefits of education. Learning and teaching strategies are used to raise self-esteem, develop confidence, independence and language and communication skills in a natural environment.
We work on the Avishayes school site but also use local woodland nearby, with permission from the land-owners. We go out in all weathers, exploring and learning about the seasons and environment changes. Suitable waterproof clothing is provided by the school so that children can get the most out of the messy opportunities!
The children take part in a range of activities, including identification of flora and fauna, problem-solving, games and sculpture. They are taught how to safely make a small '5 minute' fire for cooking on as well as how to build a range of shelters using basic materials. They are also taught how to use full-size adult tools such as saws, drills and pen-knives safely in order to make items such as toasting forks and tree 'cookies' (name plates made from a slice of wood and hung on a string)
An important aspect of Forest School is giving children an opportunity to take risks. However, an essential part of the Forest School Leader's role is to ensure that these risks are carefully assessed and monitored regularly. All the activities and sites used are very carefully risk-assessed and you receive further information if the children will be leaving the school site. Health and safety issues are identified in the risk assessment and children are made very clear of the expectations and boundaries. All Forest School leaders are qualified in Outdoor Education First Aid.

Ofsted Reports
Safeguarding and Wellbeing is Strong
Pupils are welcoming at Avishayes Community Primary School. There are strong
relationships between staff and pupils. Throughout the school, pupils are well cared for. Any unkind behaviour, such as bullying, is dealt with quickly. Staff know the pupils well.
Pupils feel safe are confident that staff will address any concerns if this is needed.
Support for pupils’ well-being is a strength. Pupils follow the school rules to be ready,
respectful and safe to learn.
Opportunities to develop pupils’ personal development are carefully considered. Pupils are
given opportunities to develop talents and interests. Pupils appreciate the range of clubs
on offer, such as football, gymnastics and performance poetry. School ambassadors take
their roles seriously and wear their school blazers with pride. They are strong role models
for younger pupils to follow.
Learning
The carefully designed curriculum in early years supports children to make a strong start.
The early years curriculum is ambitious and well sequenced to ensure that children’s
knowledge builds from Nursery into Reception. Knowledgeable staff ensure that learning
is engaging and purposeful. Children enjoy learning and playing together. The high
expectations of staff ensure routines are well established.
The school works closely with parents and pupils to highlight the importance of attending
school. It identifies any barriers to good attendance. The school recognises that those
pupils who are absent too often need more help to attend school regularly. As a result of
the school’s work, some pupils’ attendance is improving.
The school’s personal development programme is a strength. The school offers a wide
range of experiences for pupils both within and beyond their local community. Pupils have
a secure knowledge of fundamental British values and treat each other with respect.
We want to know how we are doing as a school so please complete the linked questionnaire so that we can continue to improve the education we can offer.
